newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end higher in dull trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end higher in dull trading.

text.p: Israeli shares closed slightly higher on Thursday with traders saying the market was expected to stabilise at its current level.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 0.30 percent, or 0.77 points, to 255.88 on all-share turnover of 99 million shekels against 126 million shekels on Wednesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.02 percent higher at 265.71.
Figures published on Thursday by the Central Bureau of Statistics show that in April the Mishtanim index gained 3.9 percent and the Maof rose 4.6 percent.

"Activity was dull today and if it was not for the Dow's rise on Wednesday the market would have closed lower. During the last few days the market recovered and now its time for a consolidation," said Yossi Weidelfeld at Eyal Securities.
On Wednesday, the Dow Jones industrial closed up more than 60 points at over 7022, within range of its March 11 record close of 7085.

"Trading was mixed and selective and the market is expected to remain at the current level in the near term unless there will be a real breakthrough in peace talks," said Yoram Ben-Yaeir at Ahrayut Investment Mangament.
Peacemaking between Israel and the Palestinians ground to a halt in March when Israel began building a 6,500-unit Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
"The market is still strong but it needs to stabilise now. The Maof shares closed almost unchanged and the main gainers were small-cap shares," Weidelfeld said.
The First International Bank of Israel was the main loser on the Maof falling 4.0 percent to 264,922. Traders noted that volume was very low at 341,483 shekels.

The most active shares were Israel Discount Bank, which gained 2.75 percent to 353 agorot on volume of 16.1 million shekels; Israel Chemicals, which rose 1.25 percent to 417 on turnover of 5.8 million shekels; and Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which gained 2.0 percent to 17,336 agorot on volume of 4.6 million shekels.
